text: Both Tasks exist now, but neither is actually running yet. This lesson resumes them for real, and treats that moment with more care than it might seem to deserve.

ALTER TASK RESUME, on both Tasks. From this moment, each one checks its schedule and its WHEN condition every five minutes, and runs its MERGE whenever the Stream actually has unconsumed data. SHOW TASKS confirms both now read started, not suspended.

Here's why this is worth double-checking rather than running reflexively. Resuming a Task that's already running, or a second renamed copy created during testing and never cleaned up, doesn't throw an error. It just quietly becomes a second active consumer of the same Stream, doing the same job the original was already doing. That's not hypothetical — it's the exact root cause this chapter's bug traces back to, two lessons from now.

To watch a real run happen, load a new batch of sample JSON, then check INFORMATION_SCHEMA dot TASK_HISTORY. It shows every run's outcome, succeeded, failed, or skipped. Skipped is healthy — it means the WHEN clause correctly found no new data and didn't bother running the MERGE. This exact function is what Lesson 14 reaches for again when something has actually gone wrong.
With both Tasks live and proven to run correctly, the pipeline itself is done. Next lesson starts building what Finance actually sees: a real view on top of the refund_events table.
